subject: Patterned credit requests from BlueLine HealthTech - follow-up & decision
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>; Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Suspected patterned top-up requests from BlueLine — initial data

Hannah / Dev —

Attaching a quick export showing a cluster of trial/top-up requests over the last 6 weeks that appear to be tied to the same credit card and overlapping IP ranges. The requesters list different account display names but the billing metadata looks linked. I flagged these as high-risk for credit-stacking/abuse.

Key notes: 
- 3 distinct account IDs (acct_112, acct_334, acct_551) with 5 trial/topup requests between 2025-11-20 and 2026-01-10.
- Billing email appears to be procurement@bluelinehealth.com across two accounts.
- Rapid token consumption within hours of top-up (~70% of credits used same day).

Attachment: usage-spike-20260112.csv

Recommend: place a temporary hold on further promo credits while we confirm whether these are legitimate separate teams or coordinated attempts. If we escalate, we'll need a single-thread contact at BlueLine and purchase documentation.

—Marissa
Senior Account Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>; Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Suspected patterned top-up requests from BlueLine — initial data

Thanks Marissa — good catch.

Please put an immediate block on issuing any promo credits to all accounts associated with the billing email while we investigate. Marissa, can you try to reach out to the customer contact and ask for:
- confirmation which teams these accounts represent and why separate accounts were created
- any purchase orders or procurement tickets if they believe these are legitimate

Dev — please pull the account-linking logs and any IP/Cookie overlap evidence and add to this thread. We should also check for previous credit reversals or abuse flags. I'll be the escalation owner for this one; loop in legal if the customer pushes.

Quoted:

Hannah

From: Jessica Cho <jessica.cho@bluelinehealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>; Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@bluelinehealth.com
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Suspected patterned top-up requests from BlueLine — initial data

Hi Hannah / Marissa —

Thanks for flagging. BlueLine has been onboarding faster than expected — multiple product teams requested separate sandboxes and different billing contacts. I can confirm these were legitimate teams (Analytics, ClinicalTrials, and DevTools). Procurement is finalizing a PO for enterprise credits but it’s delayed on our side.

I'm attaching the PO we expect to sign this week (PO_4567_BlueLine.pdf). We understand your policy, but these top-ups were intended to be short-term bridge credits while procurement finishes. Please let me know what you need to keep things moving.

Jess
Jessica Cho
Head of Platform Integrations
BlueLine HealthTech

Attachment: PO_4567_BlueLine.pdf
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Jessica Cho <jessica.cho@bluelinehealth.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>; Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 12:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Suspected patterned top-up requests from BlueLine — initial data

Jess — thanks for the quick reply and the PO. I work on the fraud & abuse team; I need a few items to validate that these are separate business units and not credit-stacking from the same org: 

1) Confirmation of distinct billing/legal entities or cost centers for each account (if possible, matching accounting reference on the PO).
2) List of account owner emails and manager approvals for each of the three account IDs (acct_112, acct_334, acct_551).
3) Any internal ticket/IT request IDs that show separate sandbox provisioning (this helps establish intent).

I’ve attached a small excerpt from our account-link log that shows the overlapping billing metadata and two matching IP ranges across recent top-ups. If you can provide the items above, we can put a short exception in place while procurement completes and clear the blocked accounts.

Attachment: account-link-log.txt

Policy note: per our promo-credit terms, multiple trial/topups from the same billing entity and IP cluster require procurement verification before an exception is approved. We are open to a controlled credit release but need the documentation above.

If we don’t get validation within 72 hours, we will decline additional promo credits because the pattern meets our abuse signal thresholds.

—Dev
Fraud & Abuse Analyst
Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Jessica Cho <jessica.cho@bluelinehealth.com>; Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>; Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 15:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Suspected patterned top-up requests from BlueLine — initial data

Jess —

Appreciate the PO and the context. We reviewed the logs and the overlap is strong. To keep you moving without exposing the platform to potential abuse, here's the decision: 

1) We will provision a one-off, limited credit of 5,000 tokens to the Analytics account (acct_112) for immediate testing.
2) Remaining pending promo/top-up requests will remain blocked until BlueLine provides the requested proof of separate legal/cost-center ownership, or a signed SOW that references the accounts.
3) If procurement can confirm the PO number and provide an invoice that matches each account's cost center within five business days, we will remove the block for those accounts and apply the enterprise credit against the new committed contract.

Marissa — please coordinate the partial credit release and track the outstanding items in the HubSpot deal (link below). Dev — preserve the audit artifacts and hand off to Legal if BlueLine disputes.

Decision note attached. I’ll move this to legal review only if BlueLine contests the blocks.

Attachments: decision-note-BlueLine.pdf

Hannah
Head of Sales Ops
Redwood Inference
